name: devloop-mcp

tools.name: browser_navigate
tools.description: Navigate the active pane to a URL (full page load). Returns the resolved URL and HTTP status. Use browser_back / browser_forward to move through history, browser_reload to refresh the same URL.

tools.name: browser_back
tools.description: Go back one entry in the active pane's history (no-op if there's nothing to go back to). Pairs with browser_forward; use browser_navigate to go to a new URL.

tools.name: browser_forward
tools.description: Go forward one entry in the active pane's history (no-op if there's nothing to go forward to). Pairs with browser_back; use browser_navigate to go to a new URL.

tools.name: browser_reload
tools.description: Reload the active pane's current page. Use browser_navigate to change URL instead.

hard.description: Ignore the cache (hard reload). Default false. Cockpit only; ignored under Puppeteer.

tools.name: browser_screenshot
tools.description: Capture a PNG screenshot of the active page. To find/target elements, prefer browser_snapshot (returns selectors).

fullPage.description: Capture the full scrollable page, not just the viewport (default false).

tools.name: browser_click
tools.description: Click the element matching a CSS selector (real mouse click). For keyboard keys use browser_press; to only hover use browser_hover.

selector.description: CSS selector of the element to click (e.g. a `ref` from browser_snapshot).

tools.name: browser_type
tools.description: Type text into the element matching a CSS selector (focuses, then types). For single keys use browser_press; for <select> use browser_select.

selector.description: CSS selector of the input/textarea to type into.

text.description: Text to type into the focused element.

tools.name: browser_eval
tools.description: Evaluate a JavaScript expression in the active page (via CDP) and return its value. Runs in the page's main world and can mutate page state. Prefer browser_snapshot for reading structure and browser_click/type for interactions.

expression.description: A JavaScript expression evaluated in the page; its result is returned (JSON-serializable values).

tools.name: browser_hover
tools.description: Hover the pointer over an element to trigger hover menus/tooltips. Does not click — use browser_click for that.

selector.description: CSS selector of the element to hover over.

tools.name: browser_scroll
tools.description: Scroll an element into view (pass selector), or scroll the window to coordinates (pass x and y). Provide a selector OR x+y, not both.

selector.description: CSS selector to scroll into view. Omit to scroll the window instead.

x.description: Window scroll-x in pixels (used when no selector).

y.description: Window scroll-y in pixels (used when no selector).

tools.name: browser_select
tools.description: Set the value of a <select> (or input) and fire input/change events. For typing free text use browser_type.

selector.description: CSS selector of the <select> or input.

value.description: The option's value attribute (not its visible label) to select.

tools.name: browser_press
tools.description: Press a single key (e.g. Enter, Escape, Tab, ArrowDown) on the page. For typing text use browser_type.

key.description: Key name to press, e.g. Enter, Escape, Tab, ArrowDown.

selector.description: Optional CSS selector to focus before pressing the key.

tools.name: browser_emulate
tools.description: Emulate a device/viewport on the active page. Pass a `device` preset, or custom `width`+`height`. `reset: true` restores a desktop viewport. For network conditions use browser_throttle instead.

device.description: Device preset to emulate. Use this OR width+height.

width.description: Custom viewport width in CSS pixels (with height).

height.description: Custom viewport height in CSS pixels (with width).

mobile.description: Emulate a mobile device (touch + mobile UA hints). Default false.

deviceScaleFactor.description: Device pixel ratio (e.g. 2 for retina). Default 1.

reset.description: Restore the default desktop viewport and clear emulation.

tools.name: browser_throttle
tools.description: Throttle the active page's network conditions to a named profile. Use `none` to clear. For viewport/device emulation use browser_emulate.

profile.description: Network profile to apply; `none` removes throttling.

tools.name: browser_clear_storage
tools.description: Clear the active page's storage — cookies, localStorage, IndexedDB, cache, service workers — for the current origin. Set allOrigins to wipe the whole browser session. Use to log out or test a fresh-user flow; reload afterward.

allOrigins.description: Wipe the entire session, not just the current origin.

tools.name: browser_wait_for_idle
tools.description: Wait until network activity settles (no requests for idleMs). Returns { ok }. To wait for a specific element/text use browser_wait_for.

idleMs.description: Quiet period with no requests that counts as idle, in ms (default 500).

timeoutMs.description: Max time to wait before giving up, in ms (default 10000).

tools.name: browser_snapshot
tools.description: Capture a structured snapshot of the active page: url, title, and the interactive + landmark elements (role, accessible name, value/state, heading level), each with a CSS selector `ref`. Pass a returned `ref` to browser_click / browser_type. Caps at 250 elements by default (raise `limit` for dense pages); `truncated:true` means the cap was hit. Prefer this over browser_screenshot to find and target elements reliably.

limit.description: Max elements to return (default 250). Raise it for dense pages (large tables / long forms) where the default truncates the snapshot.

tools.name: browser_wait_for
tools.description: Wait until a CSS selector appears or text is present on the page (e.g. after a navigation or async render). Returns { ok, waitedMs } — ok=false on timeout. To wait for the network to go quiet instead, use browser_wait_for_idle.

text.description: Substring of page text to wait for (if no selector).

timeoutMs.description: Max time to wait before giving up, in ms (default 10000).

tools.name: get_logs
tools.description: Return recent events from the unified buffer (server stdout/stderr + browser console/network/pageerror), newest last. Filter by source, stream, grep, and tail incrementally with sinceSeq. Scope to one project's logs with `app`. For events around a specific moment use get_logs_around; to triage errors first use diagnose.

source.description: Limit to one source: server, browser, or native.

stream.description: Limit to one stream, e.g. stdout, stderr, console, network, pageerror.

app.description: Scope to a specific app/project — matches a pane's label (project name) or id (see pane_list). Omit for all apps.

sinceSeq.description: Only events with seq >= this (for incremental tailing).

tools.name: get_logs_around
tools.description: Return ALL events (server + browser) within +/- windowMs of a timestamp, time-ordered — the correlation tool. E.g. the browser console error and the backend stack trace from the same moment. Timestamps come from the `ts` field on any event.

app.description: Optional: scope to one app/project (pane label or id; see pane_list).

tools.name: clear_logs
tools.description: Clear the event buffer (irreversible). Call before reproducing an issue for a clean window. Note: repro clears for you unless clear=false.

tools.name: export_bundle
tools.description: Export a shareable bug-report bundle as one JSON object: the diagnose summary, the timeline (logs), captured screenshots, a HAR of network, and repro steps if provided. For just the network log use export_har; for a quick triage use diagnose.

app.description: Scope to one app/project (pane label or id; see pane_list). Omit for all.

windowMs.description: Only include events from the last N ms (default: the whole buffer).

tools.name: diagnose
tools.description: Triage what's broken right now: group repeated errors (browser console/page errors + server errors) with counts, list failed/4xx-5xx network requests, and return a one-line summary. Start here before digging through get_logs.

windowMs.description: Only consider events from the last N ms (default: all).

app.description: Scope to one app/project (pane label or id).

tools.name: export_har
tools.description: Export captured network requests as a HAR 1.2 document (importable into Chrome DevTools / Charles). Covers ALL requests (the full network ring, independent of DEVLOOP_NET_THRESHOLD — bodies kept for the curated subset: failures + status ≥ threshold). To browse requests in JSON use get_network.

app.description: Scope to one app/project (pane label or id; see pane_list). Omit for all.

tools.name: get_network
tools.description: List captured network requests (the full ring — every request, independent of DEVLOOP_NET_THRESHOLD). Each row has method/url/status/timing/headers (bodies for the curated subset). Unlike get_logs (curated timeline only); for an importable HAR file use export_har.

grep.description: Substring match on the request line (status/method/url).

app.description: Scope to one app/project (pane label or id).

tools.name: dev_start
tools.description: Start a dev server and tee its logs into the buffer. Three ways to specify it: (1) `project` — a saved registry project (resolves cmd/cwd); (2) explicit `cmd`+`cwd`; (3) neither — `cwd` defaults to the server's directory and `cmd` is auto-detected from package.json. Explicit cmd/cwd override the project's. Stop it with dev_stop; check it with dev_status.

project.description: Name of a saved project (see project_list).

cmd.description: Full dev command. If omitted, auto-detected from package.json.

cwd.description: Project directory. Defaults to the server's cwd.

tools.name: dev_stop
tools.description: Stop the running dev server (SIGTERM). Returns whether one was running. Start one with dev_start.

tools.name: project_list
tools.description: List saved projects (name, cwd, cmd, url) from the registry. Add with project_add, remove with project_remove.

tools.name: project_add
tools.description: Save (or replace) a project in the registry so you can dev_start it by name. Replaces any existing project with the same name.

name.description: Unique project name (used to dev_start it later).

url.description: Default URL to open in the browser pane (optional).

tools.name: project_remove
tools.description: Remove a saved project from the registry by name (irreversible; doesn't stop a running server). List names with project_list.

name.description: Name of the saved project to remove (see project_list).

tools.name: pane_list
tools.description: List browser panes (multi-target): each has id, url, active. The active pane is what browser_*/repro act on. Switch with pane_select. (Cockpit only.)

tools.name: pane_new
tools.description: Open a new browser pane and make it active. Optionally navigate it to a URL and/or scope it to a project. Pass a saved `project` (resolves cwd/cmd/url/name), or explicit `cwd`/`cmd`/`label`, to scope the pane — cwd isolates its storage partition and names it. With none of these it's a blank, unscoped pane. To switch panes use pane_select; to close use pane_close. (Cockpit only.)

url.description: Optional URL to open (else the project's URL, else a blank pane).

project.description: Name of a saved project to scope this pane to (see project_list).

cwd.description: Project directory to scope the pane to (isolates its storage partition).

cmd.description: Dev command to associate with the pane (used by a later dev_start).

label.description: Display name for the pane (defaults to the project name or cwd basename).

tools.name: pane_select
tools.description: Make a pane active so subsequent browser_*/repro calls target it. Find ids with pane_list. (Cockpit only.)

id.description: Id of the pane to activate (from pane_list).

tools.name: pane_close
tools.description: Close a browser pane by id (irreversible). To detach a pane into its own window instead, use pane_pop. (Cockpit only.)

id.description: Id of the pane to close (from pane_list).

tools.name: pane_pop
tools.description: Detach a pane into its own standalone window (to view targets side-by-side). Closing that window re-docks the pane. pane_close removes it. (Cockpit only.)

id.description: Id of the pane to pop out (from pane_list).

tools.name: pane_set_label
tools.description: Set a pane's display label (the tab name). Also what `app` filters match in get_logs/diagnose. (Cockpit only.)

id.description: Id of the pane to label (from pane_list).

label.description: New display label (e.g. the project name).

tools.name: dev_status
tools.description: Report whether the dev server is running, plus its cmd/cwd/pid. Start/stop with dev_start/dev_stop.

tools.name: native_open
tools.description: Open a native target for the active pane (Expo/React Native): the iOS simulator or the Android device mirror. browser_* (snapshot/click/type/scroll/press/screenshot) then drive the native app via idb/adb, and JS + native logs stream to the timeline. Cockpit-only (needs the Electron app + a booted simulator/emulator). Returns ok:false with a reason if the device/tooling isn't ready. Build the app first with native_build; close with native_close.

platform.description: Which native target to open: ios (simulator) or android (emulator mirror).

tools.name: native_close
tools.description: Close the active native target; browser_* route back to the pane's web content. (Cockpit only.) Open one with native_open.

tools.name: native_build
tools.description: Build + launch the native dev build for the active pane (`expo run:ios` / `expo run:android`); output streams to the timeline. Cockpit-only, local build. Needs the native toolchain (Xcode for iOS; Android SDK + `adb` + a JDK + `$ANDROID_HOME` for Android). If the Android toolchain isn't set up it returns `started:false` with a checklist of exactly what to install, instead of failing cryptically. After it boots, use native_open to drive it.

platform.description: Which platform to build: ios or android.

cwd.description: Project directory to build; defaults to the active pane's project.

tools.name: native_doctor
tools.description: Report native readiness without building or opening anything: iOS simulator interactions, Android device interactions, and the Android local build toolchain — each a ✓/✗ checklist with the fix for anything missing. Cockpit-only, read-only. Re-probes live each call — run it after installing a missing tool to confirm it's resolved before native_build / native_open, or proactively before a long build. Returns { ios, androidInteractions, androidBuild }, each { ready, checks, summary }. native_build to build; native_open to drive a device.

tools.name: ext_list
tools.description: List Chrome extensions (loaded + disabled): id, name, version, enabled. (Cockpit only.) Install with ext_install, toggle with ext_set_enabled.

tools.name: ext_install
tools.description: Install a Chrome extension from a Web Store id or URL (downloads from the Web Store). Returns the updated list. (Cockpit only.) Remove with ext_remove.

input.description: Extension id (32 chars) or a Chrome Web Store URL.

tools.name: ext_remove
tools.description: Remove (uninstall/unload) a Chrome extension by id (irreversible for store extensions). (Cockpit only.) To keep it but turn it off, use ext_set_enabled.

tools.name: ext_set_enabled
tools.description: Enable or disable a Chrome extension by id without uninstalling. Returns the updated list. (Cockpit only.) To uninstall entirely, use ext_remove.

enabled.description: true to enable, false to disable.

tools.name: repro
tools.description: One-shot reproduce-and-correlate: clear the buffer (unless clear=false), perform one action OR a sequence in order, wait for async console/network/server events to land, then return EVERYTHING that happened on both sides plus per-step results and an errors summary. Use a sequence for flows like navigate → click → type → click submit.

actions.description: Sequence of actions performed in order. Use this OR `action`.

text.description: for kind=type, or kind=wait (text to wait for)

action.description: A single action (convenience for a one-step sequence). Ignored if `actions` is given.

text.description: for kind=type, or kind=wait (text to wait for)

waitFor.description: How to wait after each action: 'settle' = fixed sleep; 'networkidle' = wait until no network activity (more reliable for slow/streaming). Default 'settle'.

settleMs.description: Fixed wait after the FINAL action for waitFor=settle (default 1000).

stepSettleMs.description: Fixed wait BETWEEN steps for waitFor=settle (default 300).

idleMs.description: Quiet period that counts as idle for waitFor=networkidle (default 500).

timeoutMs.description: Max wait for waitFor=networkidle before giving up (default 10000).

continueOnError.description: Keep going if a step fails (default false: stop after the failing step).
